title: Shadow-channel Experimentation Framework and Telemetry Contract
author: Maya Chen
content:
Summary

This document defines Redwood's Shadow-channel Experimentation Framework (SEF) and the accompanying telemetry contract used to run non-invasive experiments across the serving runtime. SEF lets engineers validate scheduler and kernel changes, batching strategies, and caching heuristics by mirroring live requests into an isolated execution path (the shadow channel) without affecting production responses.

Goals
- Enable high-confidence performance and correctness experiments using live traffic.
- Standardize telemetry so experiment results are comparable across kernels, schedulers, and topologies.
- Provide an operator-safe runbook for starting, observing, and rolling back experiments.

Non-goals
- SEF is not a canary rollout mechanism for user-facing traffic (use the rollout service for canaries).
- SEF does not modify customer-facing outputs; quality validation must use offline evals or compare-only decoders.

When to use SEF
1. Kernel-level performance patches that require realistic traffic shaping.
2. Scheduler policy changes impacting admission, preemption, or slot assignment.
3. KV cache prefetch/hint algorithms where hit/miss patterns are critical.
4. New batching heuristics or continuous-batching changes.

Architecture Overview

SEF has three main logical components: Mirror, Shadow Executor, and Aggregation/Verifier.
- Mirror (mirror-proxy): intercepts an incoming request and clones a deterministic copy of the request context and tokens. Mirrors run in the request ingress plane and annotate requests with a correlation_id.
- Shadow Executor (shadow-exec): a sandboxed runtime instance (container-level isolation) that consumes mirrored traffic. Shadow-exec may load alternative kernels, scheduler flags, or quantization profiles. It returns telemetry only; outputs are discarded or stored in a private experiment index.
- Aggregation/Verifier (exp-agg): aggregates shadow telemetry, computes experiment metrics (latency delta, kernel time, queue time, kvcache hit breakdown, token throughput), and performs quality checks. exp-agg produces a report stored in the experiments index and notifies Slack/Confluence hooks.

Key properties
- Non-intrusive: shadow paths must not alter production responses or resource quotas used for live serving.
- Budgeted: experiments must be assigned a budget (tokens/sec or % of cluster capacity). If the shadow budget is exceeded, the mirror-proxy drops mirrored traffic for that experiment.
- Deterministic correlation: all mirrored requests share a correlation_id prefix to link production and shadow telemetry.

Telemetry Contract (required fields)
Every shadow-exec must emit the following fields for each mirrored request (JSON lines to exp-agg):
- correlation_id: string (prefix links to production request)
- experiment_id: string
- timestamp_utc: iso8601 string
- stage_durations_ms: list (ingress, queue, kernel_dispatch, kernel_exec, decoder, kvcache_lookup) encoded as CSV of numbers
- kernel_signature: string (kernel name + variant + commit)
- scheduler_profile: string (policy name + profile hash)
- kvcache_stats: csv (hits, misses, prefetches, eviction_count)
- cpu_usec: integer
- gpu_usec: integer
- memory_bytes: integer
- status: ok | exec_error | resource_throttled | timed_out
- sampled_trace_id: optional string (links to full trace in tracing system)

Metric definitions (computed by exp-agg)
- shadow_p95_latency_ms: 95th percentile of end-to-end shadow latency
- delta_p95_ms: shadow_p95 - prod_p95 (linked by correlation_id)
- kernel_time_ratio: kernel_exec / end_to_end
- kv_hit_rate: hits / (hits + misses)
- resource_overhead_percent: (gpu_usec + cpu_usec equivalent) / prod_resource_usage

SLO and safety thresholds for experiments
- Max allowed delta_p95_ms: +5ms for latency-sensitive tiers, +20ms for best-effort experiments. Exceeding triggers automatic suspension.
- Max resource overhead percent: 25% (across aggregate traffic).
- Error budget for exec_error: 0.2% of mirrored requests per hour.

Experiment lifecycle (operator steps)
1. Create experiment metadata in experiments-service with experiment_id, owner, target clusters, budget (tokens/sec or %), and risk classification (low/medium/high).
2. Push experiment config to mirror-proxy: rdinfer-mirrorctl create --id <experiment_id> --budget 50rps --target shadow-cluster:shadow-v2 --policy sample:1/1000
3. Validate mirror can deliver minimal load by enabling a 0.1% sample on a low-traffic route.
4. Start shadow-exec job: k8s apply -f shadow-exec-<experiment_id>.yaml. Shadow-exec must run with nodeSelector=isolated-exec and resource limits set to the budgeted rate.
5. Wait for stable telemetry for 30 minutes. Run exp-agg quick-check: exp-agg check --experiment <id> --metrics delta_p95_ms,kernel_time_ratio,kv_hit_rate
6. Run benchmark harness (see Benchmark protocol below) or replay stored requests for reproducibility.
7. If metrics are within thresholds, scale up to the target budget incrementally (x2 every 30m). Monitor SLOs and resource overhead.
8. Conclude experiment and archive report. For negative results, follow the Rollback and postmortem procedure.

Operator runbook (quick actions)
- Suspend experiment: rdinfer-mirrorctl suspend --id <experiment_id>
- Resume experiment: rdinfer-mirrorctl resume --id <experiment_id>
- Emergency stop (immediate): rdinfer-mirrorctl kill --id <experiment_id> (drops mirror; does not delete artifacts)
- Collect traces for a sample: exp-agg collect-traces --experiment <id> --sample 100

Benchmark protocol (for synthetic verification)
Purpose: ensure shadow-exec results align with synthetic bench suite. Use the runtime benchmarking harness with mirrored request signatures.
Steps:
1. Rehydrate a 1-hour traffic window (production) into the benchmark harness: benchctl replay --source s3://prod-traces/2026-01-15/route-X --realtime=false --rate-scale 1.0 --target shadow-exec:5000
2. Run with the kernel variant under test and capture the same telemetry contract.
3. Compare bench outputs to exp-agg aggregated metrics using bench-compare: bench-compare --baseline prod --candidate shadow --metrics delta_p95_ms,kernel_time_ratio
Acceptance criteria:
- delta_p95_ms within the SLO defined above
- kernel_time_ratio difference < 10%
- no new exec_error class > 0.05%

Safety and resource isolation patterns
- Shadow-exec pods must be scheduled onto a dedicated taint:isolation=true node pool to prevent noisy neighbor effects. Use tolerations only for exp operator service account.
- ResourceLimits on shadow-exec pods: cpu=4, memory=16Gi, gpu=1 (or set GPU quota via device plugin).
- Throttling: mirror-proxy enforces an absolute max RPS per experiment to avoid runaway costs. Defaults: 100rps per experiment in hosted clusters.

Data retention and privacy
- Shadow payloads must strip PII before persisting to experiment indexes. Use the redact pipeline: redact-agent --policy exp-standard --in /tmp/exp-raw.json --out /tmp/exp-redacted.json
- Experiment telemetry retention: 90 days. Aggregated reports archived indefinitely.

Rollbacks and postmortem
- If an experiment breaches thresholds, suspend mirror immediately and mark experiment status=halted.
- Capture a forensics bundle: exp-agg bundle --id <experiment_id> --output /tmp/forensics.tar.gz
- Create an incident with severity matched to risk_classification. Notify owners and reviewers.

Appendix A: Example shadow-exec manifest (Kubernetes)
---
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: shadow-exec-<experiment_id>
  labels:
    app: shadow-exec
    experiment: "<experiment_id>"
spec:
  replicas: 2
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: shadow-exec
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: shadow-exec
    spec:
      nodeSelector:
        node-pool: shadow-isolated
      tolerations:
      - key: "isolation"
        operator: "Equal"
        value: "true"
        effect: "NoSchedule"
      containers:
      - name: shadow-exec
        image: rdinfer/shadow-exec:stable-2026-01
        resources:
          limits:
            cpu: "4"
            memory: "16Gi"
            nvidia.com/gpu: "1"
        env:
        - name: EXPERIMENT_ID
          value: "<experiment_id>"
---

Appendix B: Minimal exp-agg check output (JSON lines)
{"experiment_id":"exp-abc123", "metric":"delta_p95_ms", "value": 3.8, "threshold": 5.0}
{"experiment_id":"exp-abc123", "metric":"kernel_time_ratio", "value": 0.62}
